system.description:
While any wheelchair can be used in a fight, the combat wheelchair is specifically designed for quick, sharp movements, mobility, and a wide and low center of gravity. Rather than have a high back with handles like a push wheelchair, the combat wheelchair has a very low, padded back to protect the lumbar region and allow for maximum upper body movement. The shield-like drive wheels are also tilted inward at the top and outward at the bottom to increase stability, and one’s legs and waist are strapped into the wheelchair to ensure they can’t be easily pulled out of it. Finally, it has both the traditional front caster wheels and also a rear caster wheel, making it very difficult to flip or knock over.

While in a combat wheelchair, traveling up slopes counts as difficult terrain. You gain an additional 15ft of movement when traveling downhill. Getting into or out of the combat wheelchair requires an action to buckle or unbuckle your legs and lower body, in addition to half your movement to enter or exit the chair, just as if you were standing up from prone.

While strapped into a combat wheelchair you gain a +1 bonus to AC and take no damage if you move across volatile, but shallow, surfaces. Such as a puddle of acid from a thrown flask.

In addition to functioning as a mobility aid, the armored combat wheelchair includes a latching steel plate that encases your legs and lower body. It functions in a similar way to the traditional combat wheelchair with two caveats. It takes two actions to get into or out of the chair, and so long as you are wearing light or medium armor you gain a +2 bonus to your AC while secured in the armored combat wheelchair.
